quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: When a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must you do?

options.text: Follow what other cars are doing instead of the guard's instructions.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.explanation: Always follow the directions of a crossing guard, sign, or police officer in a school zone. Slow down and drive with extra caution when directed to do so.

questions.question: You must yield to children playing in the streets.
questions.explanation: You must drive with extreme caution where children are present. Slow down near schools, playgrounds, and in residential areas.

questions.question: On a slippery road, your following distance should be:
questions.explanation: You need more distance to stop on a slippery road than on a dry road. Keep a longer distance between your car and the car ahead on slippery roads.

questions.question: Before backing up, you should always check behind your car for bikes, tricycles, and small children.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your car for bikes, tricycles, and small children before you get in your car to back up. This is especially important if you drive a large vehicle like a van or truck.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard flashers when your car breaks down on the highway. Move as far off the road as possible. Lift your hood to show other drivers that your vehicle is disabled.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if you don't see any other cars.
Signal only if other cars are visible.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if you don't see any other cars.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb. Make this a habit and do not skip signaling even when the road appears empty.

questions.question: Which is a sign of a drunk driver?
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving slower than other cars, jerking motions, and sudden stops.

questions.question: When taking medicine, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor if it will affect your driving.
Open your window and drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor if it will affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your ability to drive. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist about how medicine will affect your driving, especially tranquilizers or sedatives.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: Take breaks every hour during long trips. If possible, share driving with another person so you can rest while they drive.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: When you are on a hill or curve.
When there is a solid line next to your lane.
When there is a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross it to change lanes. A solid line means you cannot pass. Only change lanes when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What should you do when you see other drivers acting or reacting with anger?
questions.explanation: When other drivers are acting angrily, stay safe by moving away from them. Avoid eye contact and do not make gestures that could anger them. Slow down, move to another lane, or do whatever you can to keep yourself safe.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of a steep hill ahead. You should slow down to avoid crashes and brake problems.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road curves to the right and then to the left. Slow down to safely navigate these curves.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop if other cars are coming.
Come to a complete stop and go when it is safe.
Go through the intersection slowly without always stopping.
Stop only if cars are on the other road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must stop completely. Let cars and pedestrians in or entering the intersection pass first. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Before turning, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn. This warns other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no warning signals, you should slow down, look, and listen.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with no warning lights or gates, slow down and look both ways. Listen for a train. Cross only when it is safe.

questions.question: Why should you not follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the car's turn signals.
You may not see the car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the car ahead stops suddenly, you may not have enough time to stop and could crash.

questions.question: What problems do worn or bald tires cause?

options.text: The tires are more likely to hydroplane.

questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires make it harder to turn and increase your stopping distance. They also increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: At a stop sign with no crosswalk, must you stop before entering the intersection?
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, stop at the stop line if there is one. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before the intersection.

questions.question: Why is night driving more challenging?

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road at night.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you can only see as far as your headlights shine. This makes it difficult to judge how far away other cars are and how fast they are going.
